Contact the Free DFW Roofing Line

Calling is the quickest way: the assistant answers every hour of the day. If you would rather type, the form below goes to a roofing company that works in your part of DFW, and it calls you back.

Call (469) 649-7066 Send the form
  1. Home
  2. Contact

Send a roof request

Fill in the four required fields and add a note if it helps. A roofing company that takes calls in your town will phone you back. If the roof is leaking right now, call (469) 649-7066 instead; a form cannot get anyone moving tonight.

Only the roofer who phones you back sees what you send. It is never sold. Read the privacy policy and the terms.

Ways to reach the line

Phone, any hour

(469) 649-7066. An automated assistant answers day and night, every day of the year. Say you need a roofer, describe the problem, and name your town.

The form on this page

Best for work that can wait: an aging roof, a bid you want compared, or a commercial roof that needs a look before the next storm season.

Facebook

The line also has a Facebook page linked at the bottom of every page. For roof help, the phone gets you to a roofer faster than a message.

What to have ready

  • Your address or nearest cross streets, and the town (city limits matter for permits).
  • What you see: a stain, a drip, missing shingles, dented gutters, hail in the yard, a limb on the roof.
  • When it started, and the date of the storm if one caused it.
  • Whether you have already called your insurance company, and the claim number if you have one.
  • Roughly how old the roof is, if you know.

About this line: DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofing contractor. It answers your call and connects you with an independent local roofing company, which inspects, quotes and does the work, and which you pay directly. Companies may pay a referral fee. Calling the line costs you nothing. See how a call is handled.

Questions North Texas homeowners ask

Is it better to call or to send the form?

Call if water is coming in, if a limb is on the roof, or if you want to reach a roofer as soon as possible. The assistant transfers you while you are still on the line. The form suits a problem that can wait a day or two, such as an old roof you want looked at or a second opinion on a bid. Either way, the request lands with a locally owned roofer near you. See how the line works.

Who receives what I type in the form?

Your name, phone number, town, the type of help you picked and your note go to one locally owned DFW roofer that serves your town, which then phones you. The line does not sell your details. The privacy policy explains what is kept and how to ask for it to be removed.

Can I email the line or stop by in person?

No. DFW Expert Roofers is a phone line and website with no walk-in office and no public email. The phone and this form are the two ways to reach it. Any visit to your home is made by the roofing company you are connected with, and it should tell you who is coming and when.

Can I send photos of the damage?

Not through this form. Keep your photos on your phone, dated, and show them to the roofer when it calls or visits, and to your insurance adjuster if you file a claim. Take them from the ground and from inside the house only; never climb up to get a better angle. The hail claim checklist lists which shots help most.

Rather talk it through? Call now

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.

Call (469) 649-7066

  • Picks up day or nightStorms here often hit in the evening. The assistant answers at 2 a.m. the same as at noon.
  • Costs you nothingThe line sends no bill. Any price you hear comes from the roofer, and you can ask for it on paper.
  • Check before you hireTexas issues no roofing license, so ask for an insurance certificate, a written contract and the permit your city requires.
  • Your call to makeListen to what the roofer found, read the estimate, and say yes only when it adds up.
